Key design decisions recorded (against the design doc, disclosed):

- **`records` (index row / dossier total) = records placed here** —
  the K4 §5.2 verbatim definition ("published observation-level
  records placed here"). A record counts in every ancestor on its
  chain exactly once. The D-K4-3 thresholds apply to this figure.
  The declared-leg (a record declared here but located elsewhere)
  shows on the dossier as the "declared here, located elsewhere"
  disclosure (K4 §3.4) — it does not make a page.
- **D-K4-3 applied verbatim (not re-decided):** county (US level):
  every county with ≥1 record gets a page. US place: ≥10 records,
  **or** any non-site evidence (research-dossier packet, agenda
  tenants, CCOPS, city-scoped sources — non-site per K4 §3.2's
  I8-class evidence). Non-US admin-1: ≥10 records. US admin-1
  (incl. DC, PR, VI — D-K4-4 keeps PR/VI under `iso3166-1:US`):
  no threshold (all with ≥1 record, matching the "51 states + DC +
  PR/VI" level table). Country: all with ≥1 record. National keys:
  country threshold.
- **Non-site evidence detection:** a `research_dossiers/*.json`
  packet whose jurisdiction names resolve to a place key through the
  landed `jurisdiction.lookup` contract (K4 §5.4) — the row uses the
  landed lookup, never a second resolver. US counties have no
  non-site route under D-K4-3 (county floor is already ≥1 record).
- **Slug paths (K4 §3.1 verbatim):** country → lowercase alpha-3
  (`usa`); admin-1 → `<a3>/<sub-lowercase>` (`usa/ca`, `gbr/eng`);
  US county → `<a3>/<sub>/<namelsad-slug>-<geoid>`
  (`usa/ca/los-angeles-county-06037`); US place → same with the
  place NAMELSAD + place GEOID. National keys →
  `<a3>/<scheme-family>-<code>` slug (no national dossiers in the
  fixture/release set yet — the scheme prefix is the collision guard
  for when I8 lands them). `web/jurisdiction_key_map.json` maps
  canonical jkey → slug path + names so consumers never re-derive.
- **The "dossier set" the ticket's roll-up rule sums is the
  page-eligible set.** Child-page sums plus records placed only at
  the parent equal the parent's total; keys below threshold keep
  full ancestor-chain bookkeeping in the index (`children` tables
  show their counts; they get no page and no per-dossier JSON).
- **Unplaced is never a key.** Dossier-side bookkeeping uses a
  module-level sentinel (`UNPLACED_KEY`), never a registry key and
  never a fabricated jurisdiction. Every unplaced row keeps its
  `placement_check` reason (R1/R6/R7/R8 vocabulary).
- **Gap `subject_id` re-key:** legacy `jurisdiction:<slug>` rows map
  to `jurisdiction:<jkey>` via the slug history (the K4 §8.1 seed
  table covers every legacy dossier slug the current exports emit).
  Unmappable rows are
  recorded under `rekey_notes` in the artifact, never dropped
  silently. New gap rows emit `jurisdiction:<jkey>`.
- **`unresolved` → `unplaced`:** new release trees and the new web
  surface use `unplaced`; the export no longer mints a flat
  `unresolved` dossier. Legacy `unresolved/` release trees stay
  readable (immutable trees are never rewritten; the slug-history
  seed maps `unresolved` → `unplaced` for the web surface).
- **Page types (K4-P7/row-328 registry):** P35.50's page-type
  registry has not landed; this row records its intended classes here
  so they can be registered with the routes: `/dossier/<path>/`,
  `/dossier/`, `/dossier/unplaced/`, the history stubs — T1
  (public, zero-JS); the kept `/dossier/<path>/print/` — T0.
- **Old `dossiers.json`/`dossier_index.json` monoliths die** per K4
  §5.3 step 6 (`web/dossiers/<slug-path>.json` + `index.json` v2);
  the release writer and `web/src/lib/data.ts` are updated in the
  same change so nothing references the dead paths.
